Subject: Invoicing cadence and PO — Sequoia Health

Hi Monica,

Thanks again for the demo. Procurement asked that we propose quarterly invoicing (one consolidated invoice per quarter) and a 90-day payment window to align with our fiscal distribution. We have a signed PO (attached) and are ready to move forward, but those two items are blockers for our AR team.

Can Redwood accept quarterly invoicing + Net-90 for the first 12 months? If not, please let me know what compromises we can propose — Sequoia is willing to provide a 30% upfront payment if that helps.

Meredith

Hi Meredith — great to get the PO. Appreciate the context on your fiscal cadence.

Short answer: quarterly invoicing + Net-90 is not our standard for enterprise new customers (we usually require Net-30 or Net-60 plus deposit for extended terms). That said, we can propose a conditional pilot for 12 months with the following compromise:
- 30% upfront payment on contract execution
- Quarterly invoicing for usage/overage after the deposit is applied
- Remaining balance payable Net-60 from invoice date (not Net-90)
- Credit limit and usage caps enforced; if usage exceeds forecast, payment terms revert to Net-30

I will loop in Deals Desk/Finance for executive review — copying them now. Can you confirm that Sequoia is comfortable with a 30% deposit to unblock the contract? If yes, I’ll submit for provisional approval.

Thanks,
Monica Patel

Date: Fri, 19 Jun 2026 08:30:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Sequoia Health — invoicing cadence & interim payment structure (escalation)

Team — escalating for exec sign-off. Summary: Sequoia Health (Prospect) requests quarterly invoicing + Net-90 for first 12 months; provided signed PO. AE proposes 30% deposit + quarterly invoices + Net-60 for remaining balance.

Risk/thoughts:
- Quarterly + Net-90 materially increases DSO. Without upfront, collection risk high.
- Sequoia has B2B healthcare payment history but limited public AR data — recommend credit check and 30% deposit to mitigate.
- Operational impact: billing consolidation and one invoice per quarter is fine, but credit hold/usage caps must be enforced in billing system.

Requested approval: temporary exception to standard terms to allow quarterly invoicing for 12 months provided: 30% deposit at signing, Net-60 on quarter invoices, $250k credit cap, monthly usage reporting, and automatic revert to standard terms on breach.

I’ve attached the term sheet and a short DD summary. Requesting Jonas or Finance lead to approve or propose final conditional language.

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Head, Deal Desk | Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com

Attachments: deal-due-diligence-summary.pdf, redwood-term-sheet-v2.docx
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwoodinference.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwoodinference.com>, naomi_feldman <naomi_feldman@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2026 09:17:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Escalation — Sequoia Health invoicing exception

Thanks for the summary. Approved provisionally with the following binding conditions:
1) 30% deposit on contract signature (non-refundable, applied to first quarter).
2) Quarterly consolidated invoices thereafter with Net-60 payment terms. Net-90 is not approved.
3) Credit exposure capped at $250,000; any forecasted usage above approved cap requires prepayment for the delta.
4) Customer to provide monthly consumption reports; overages billed at standard rates on the quarterly invoice.
5) Approval valid for an initial 12-month pilot; after 12 months, terms automatically evaluate to standard Net-30 unless extended by finance.
6) SLA credit exposure reduced to 25% for the pilot period.

Please confirm language in the contract addendum and provide a signed PO + deposit confirmation before provisioning. Monica — once you have Meredith’s confirmation of the deposit and the PO, forward for DocuSign.

Jonas Weber
Director, Revenue Operations | Redwood Inference

Hi Meredith — good news: Finance has provisionally approved a 12-month pilot with quarterly invoices, subject to the conditions below. Please review and confirm so we can issue the DocuSign: 

Conditions (as approved):
- 30% deposit due at signing (applied to Q1).
- Quarterly consolidated invoices thereafter, Net-60 on invoice date (Net-90 is not approved).
- $250k credit exposure cap; prepay required for forecasted usage above the cap.
- Monthly consumption reporting by Sequoia (to be shared with Redwood billing).
- Pilot term: 12 months; automatic review at renewal.

Next steps:
1) Please reply to confirm acceptance of the deposit and the conditions.
2) I will send the DocuSign package (term addendum + SOW).
3) Once deposit clears and DocuSign completes, we’ll kick off provisioning.
